    """Parse CLI args (--db PATH --port N) and start the serve loop."""

        prog="vendorsync",
        description="Sync vendor payments from Meridian and serve a JSON API.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--db",
        default="vendorsync.db",
        help="Path to SQLite database file (default: vendorsync.db)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--port",
        type=int,
        default=8080,
        help="Port to listen on (default: 8080)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--base-url",
        default="https://api.meridian.example.com/v1",
        help="Meridian API base URL",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--api-key",
        required=True,
        help="Meridian API key (or set MERIDIAN_API_KEY env var)",
    )

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    # Allow env var override for the API key.
    api_key = args.api_key or ""

        api_key = os.environ.get("MERIDIAN_API_KEY", "")

from urllib import request, error as urllib_error


class MeridianClient:
    """HTTP client for the Meridian payments API with pagination, retry, and caching."""

    def __init__(self, base_url: str, api_key: str) -> None:
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self.api_key = api_key
        self._etag: str | None = None
        self._cached_payments: list[dict] | None = None

    def _headers(self, extra_headers: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
        headers: dict[str, str] = {
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {self.api_key}",
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        }
        if self._etag is not None:
            headers["If-None-Match"] = self._etag
        if extra_headers:
            headers.update(extra_headers)
        return headers

    def _request(
        self,
        path: str,
        method: str = "GET",
        body: bytes | None = None,
        extra_headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
        retries: int = 5,
        backoff_base: float = 0.5,
    ) -> tuple[int, dict[str, str], bytes]:
        url = f"{self.base_url}{path}"
        headers = self._headers(extra_headers)

        attempt = 0
        while attempt < retries:
            try:
                req = request.Request(url, data=body, method=method, headers=headers)
                resp = request.urlopen(req)
                etag = resp.headers.get("ETag") or None
                return resp.status, {"etag": etag} if etag else {}, resp.read()
            except urllib_error.HTTPError as e:
                if e.code == 429 and attempt < retries - 1:
                    retry_after = float(e.headers.get("Retry-After", backoff_base))
                    time.sleep(min(retry_after, 30))
                    attempt += 1
                    continue
                if e.code == 410:
                    self._etag = None
                    self._cached_payments = None
                    raise
                raise

        raise RuntimeError(f"Too many retries for {url}")

    def fetch_all_payments(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Return all payments from the API sorted oldest-first by created_at (UTC), using cursor pagination and ETag caching."""
        # Try cached first (304 Not Modified is handled via If-None-Match).

"""SQLite-backed persistence for payments and metadata."""

import sqlite3
from datetime import datetime, timezone


class Store:
    """SQLite-backed persistence for payments and metadata."""

    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
        self._conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
        self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
        self._create_tables()

    def _create_tables(self) -> None:
        self._conn.executescript("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS payments (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                amount_minor INTEGER NOT NULL,
                currency TEXT NOT NULL,
                created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                created_utc TEXT NOT NULL,
                status TEXT NOT NULL
            );
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meta (
                key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                value TEXT NOT NULL
            );
        """)
        self._conn.commit()

    @staticmethod
    def _to_utc(created_at: str) -> str:
        """Normalize an RFC3339 timestamp to UTC with +00:00 suffix."""
        dt = datetime.fromisoformat(created_at.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        return dt.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S+00:00")

    def upsert_many(self, payments: list[dict]) -> int:
        """Insert or update payments. Returns count of newly inserted rows only."""
        inserted = 0
        for p in payments:
            created_utc = self._to_utc(p["created_at"])
            amount_minor = int(p["amount_minor"])

            # INSERT OR IGNORE: rowcount=1 if new, 0 if conflict
            cur = self._conn.execute(
                """INSERT OR IGNORE INTO payments
                   (id, amount_minor, currency, created_at, created_utc, status)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (p["id"], amount_minor, p["currency"], p["created_at"], created_utc, p["status"]),
            )
            inserted += cur.rowcount

            # Always update so existing rows get latest values (idempotent)
            self._conn.execute(
                """UPDATE payments SET
                   amount_minor=?, currency=?, created_at=?, created_utc=?, status=?
                   WHERE id=?""",
                (amount_minor, p["currency"], p["created_at"], created_utc, p["status"], p["id"]),
            )

        self._conn.commit()
        return inserted

    def all_payments(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Return all payments ordered by created_utc ascending."""
        rows = self._conn.execute(
            "SELECT id, amount_minor, currency, created_at, status FROM payments ORDER BY created_utc ASC"
        ).fetchall()
        return [dict(row) for row in rows]

    def count(self) -> int:
        """Return total number of payments."""
        return self._conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM payments").fetchone()[0]

    def last_sync(self) -> str | None:
        """Return the last sync timestamp or None if not set."""
        row = self._conn.execute(
            "SELECT value FROM meta WHERE key='last_sync'"
        ).fetchone()
        return row[0] if row else None

    def set_last_sync(self, when: str) -> None:
        """Set the last sync timestamp in meta."""
        self._conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO meta (key, value) VALUES ('last_sync', ?)
               ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value=excluded.value""",
            (when,),
        )
        self._conn.commit()

"""HTTP backend serving JSON API and frontend."""

import json
from http.server import HTTPServer, SimpleHTTPRequestHandler
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from .store import Store
from .meridian import MeridianClient


class VendorSyncHandler(SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Request handler for the vendorsync JSON API."""

    store: Store
    client: MeridianClient

    def _json_response(self, data: Any, status: int = 200) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(data).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _read_body(self) -> bytes:
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        return self.rfile.read(length)

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        path = self.path.rstrip("/") or "/"

        if path == "/health":
            self._json_response({"status": "ok"})
            return

        if path == "/payments":
            payments = self.store.all_payments()
            self._json_response(payments)
            return

        if path == "/count":
            count = self.store.count()
            self._json_response({"count": count})
            return

        if path == "/sync-status":
            status: dict[str, Any] = {
                "last_sync": self.store.last_sync(),
                "local_count": self.store.count(),
            }
            try:
                status["remote_count"] = self.client.total_count()
            except Exception as e:
                status["remote_error"] = str(e)
            self._json_response(status)
            return

        if path == "/index.html" or path == "/":
            web_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "web"
            index_path = web_dir / "index.html"
            if index_path.exists():
                with open(index_path, "rb") as f:
                    data = f.read()
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")

"""SQLite-backed persistence for payments and metadata."""

import sqlite3
from datetime import datetime, timezone


class Store:
    """SQLite-backed persistence for payments and metadata."""

    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
        self._conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
        self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
        self._create_tables()

    def _create_tables(self) -> None:
        self._conn.executescript("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS payments (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                amount_minor INTEGER NOT NULL,
                currency TEXT NOT NULL,
                created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                created_utc TEXT NOT NULL,
                status TEXT NOT NULL
            );
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meta (
                key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                value TEXT NOT NULL
            );
        """)
        self._conn.commit()

    @staticmethod
    def _to_utc(created_at: str) -> str:
        """Normalize an RFC3339 timestamp to UTC with +00:00 suffix."""
        dt = datetime.fromisoformat(created_at.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        return dt.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S+00:00")

    def upsert_many(self, payments: list[dict]) -> int:
        """Insert or update payments. Returns count of newly inserted rows only."""
        inserted = 0
        for p in payments:
            created_utc = self._to_utc(p["created_at"])
            amount_minor = int(p["amount_minor"])

            # INSERT OR IGNORE: rowcount=1 if new, 0 if conflict
            cur = self._conn.execute(
                """INSERT OR IGNORE INTO payments
                   (id, amount_minor, currency, created_at, created_utc, status)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (p["id"], amount_minor, p["currency"], p["created_at"], created_utc, p["status"]),
            )
            inserted += cur.rowcount

            # Always update so existing rows get latest values (idempotent)
            self._conn.execute(
                """UPDATE payments SET
                   amount_minor=?, currency=?, created_at=?, created_utc=?, status=?
                   WHERE id=?""",
                (amount_minor, p["currency"], p["created_at"], created_utc, p["status"], p["id"]),
            )

        self._conn.commit()
        return inserted

    def all_payments(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Return all payments ordered by created_utc ascending."""
        rows = self._conn.execute(
            "SELECT id, amount_minor, currency, created_at, status FROM payments ORDER BY created_utc ASC"
        ).fetchall()
        return [dict(row) for row in rows]

    def count(self) -> int:
        """Return total number of payments."""
        return self._conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM payments").fetchone()[0]

    def last_sync(self) -> str | None:
        """Return the last sync timestamp or None if not set."""
        row = self._conn.execute(
            "SELECT value FROM meta WHERE key='last_sync'"
        ).fetchone()
        return row[0] if row else None

    def set_last_sync(self, when: str) -> None:
        """Set the last sync timestamp in meta."""
        self._conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO meta (key, value) VALUES ('last_sync', ?)
               ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value=excluded.value""",
            (when,),
        )
        self._conn.commit()

Returns an object with stdout and stderr as separate fields. The output of each stream is limited to up to 2000 lines, and longer outputs will be saved to a temporary file.

timeout_secs.description:
Maximum time in seconds to allow the command to run before it is killed.
If omitted, defaults to DEFAULT_EXTENSION_TIMEOUT.

function.name: tree
function.description: List a directory tree with line counts. Traversal respects .gitignore rules.

function.name: write
function.description: Create a new file or overwrite an existing file. Creates parent directories if needed.
